romans.13.p1.b1.text: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. …

romans.13.p1.b2.text: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. …

romans.13.p1.b3.text: For he is God’s servant for your good. …

romans.13.p2.b1.text: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

romans.13.p2.b2.text: Pay everyone what you owe him …

romans.13.p2.b3.text: … taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

romans.13.p3.b1.text: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

romans.13.p3.b2.text: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments …

romans.13.p3.b3.text: … are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

romans.13.p3.b4.text: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

romans.13.p4.b1.text: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

romans.13.p4.b2.text: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. …

romans.13.p4.b3.text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime …

romans.13.p4.b4.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
